items.title: Show HN: Worktable, an open-source workspace for you and your agents
items.summary: Hello HN! I built Worktable as an open-source, file-based workspace for you and your agents to create docs, plans, and build small tools. For example, you ask an agent to compare hosting options for your next side project, save the research notes, and build a calculator where you can adjust traffic and storage assumptions yourself. As a backstory, I run my Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw on a server at home and was consistently frustrated with the experience of trying to review/edit docs, share context between them, switch to other new agents, and more. In the last few months, it has become what all my daily work depends on so I decided to make a product and release it for others to use. What’s included: - Markdown, richtext, HTML, structured records as YAML - A built-in runtime and data API for HTML dashboards, calculators, planners, etc - Comments and version history - MCP connections to local, self-hosted or Worktable Cloud - Threads for you and your agents + a dedicated OpenClaw plugin for automatic replies (Hermes coming soon) - Plain files in regular folders. Same workspace format and export/import across local, self-hosted and cloud. Free local/self-hosted, AGPL. Cloud is optional. Try it with your agents. I’d love to learn what you do with it and what gets in the way. Website: https://worktable.dev Github: https://github.com/worktable/worktable-dev

Show HN: Tasket++ Simulate your Windows actions automatically-free and OS
items.summary: Tasket++ lets you define your own clicks, keystrokes, cursor positions and system operations, then replay them exactly when you want. It’s a simple Windows tool that handles repetitive workflows for you: auto‑send messages, paste text anywhere, take silent screenshots, launch or close apps, adjust volume or run your end‑of‑day shutdown sequence. Everything runs locally, with no telemetry, no cloud, and no complexity. What it can do: - Replay user‑defined cursor positions and keystrokes - Paste predefined text anywhere - Perform system actions: open files/programs, change volume, take silent screenshots, shut down, files/folders operations - Schedule tasks at a specific time, at startup, or run via desktop shortcut - Run tasks once, in loops, or indefinitely - Discreet mode: runs quietly from the tray - Use command line to autorun a task : Tasket++.exe "TaskName" <delayInSeconds (>0)> <NumberOfLoop (-1 for infinite)> - Easily share tasks between different PC : just import the .scht file located in /saved_tasks Local, portable, free, open source. Privacy intact. Fully fonctionnal, available now ! Microsoft Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/xp9cjlhwvxs49p Portable (v2.0): https://files.amirhammoutene.dev/Tasket++/2.0/Tasket++_v2.0.... Source: https://github.com/AmirHammouteneEI/ScheduledPasteAndKeys For feedback, help, suggestions, or other inquiries : contact@amirhammoutene.dev Nothing is vibe coded, I never used AI (except for the choice of UI colors suggested by Copilot). Conception is genuine, I didn't know about similar tools when I began developing it.

Show HN: TiddlyInstall – Single HTML file that makes cross-platform installers
items.summary: Hello HN, I wanted to show you some new software I designed (and Claude implemented.) It's called TiddlyInstall. TiddlyInstall is a single-page website that lets you easily build installers for all your projects. What makes TiddlyInstall unusual is there is no software to download and everything is able to work offline. Based on the project that it's inspired by: you can download TiddlyInstall as a HTML file and use it to make working binaries for Windows, Linux, and Mac. How it works: Most installers / binaries are custom per project. But with very few modifications they can be made general-purpose. Installers can be made to follow meta-data which can be vouched for by hashes in their file names, embedded data, and signatures. That means new binaries only need meta-data to be changed which can be done entirely in the browser. For the installers themselves NSIS was chosen for its amazing Windows support. Otherwise, the rest is shell scripting. I am very excited about it and would love people to try it out. All the code is open source under MIT. Feel free to report issues on the Github at http://github.com/robertsdotpm/tiddlyinstall Credits: Claude (and the authors whose works it was trained on :/) deserve huge credits for the implementation. It would have taken me months to code this all this. This project is not affiliated with TiddlyWiki -- though I am heavily inspired by that project! If anyone thinks my work is cool -- I'm currently looking for new opportunities. Feel free to reach out if there's a match (matthew@roberts.pm.)
